posts.cooked:
I shall post one of my early plans which is flawed for many reasons, not the least of which is that Ronway will soon know what it is.

The primary hurdle with any defense is going to overcoming Ronway's sheer power (and slight mintiness). Therefore, this plan is devised to use his own power against him (he is immune to slight mintiness; the power will have to suffice). Here's how it will go down:

General Butane (Matchstickman) will direct our primary defense, holding off Ronway's assault for as long as possible.

Meanwhile, Proclaimer (BlueHairedMeerkat) will launch a new forum dedicated spreading the word of Ronway's treachery. It will be loud enough to draw the attention of some of the forumites, but it will be shoddily constructed and so no one (including Ronway) will give it a second thought.

The Bezaliel (Nielzabub), will sneak off to form the Believers of the True Ronway forum. As if Ronway weren't strong enough already, it will draw out those who will proclaim their allegiance to him in hopes of basking in his mintiness. Ronway accepts their support, arming them with his own power and resources and sends them off to attack the forums.

As General Butane's defenses start to crumble, Ronway grows overconfident. As he is known to do, Ronway strikes his allies down to the last and strides in triumphantly as the remaining forumites flee or fall.

It takes a little while for Ronway to realize that the spoils are not quite as sweet as he had hoped. The remains of the forum are flimsy and hollow. And though he expended no great effort, he feels a little run down. Perhaps it is because of the things he didn't notice.

For instance, the Caster of Nets (Silverleaf) and her army of tiny crocheted ant-bots scouring the battlefield leeching Ronway's minty power from his fallen one-time allies before it could return to him. And it never really registered that the Bezaliel vanished shortly after constructing the Believers forum. Nor did he pay any heed to forumite newbie, the Indubious (XXVZ), who quietly relocated the forums into a bunker under the Proclaimer's deceptively shoddy-looking propoganda camouflage and left a cardboard forum replica for General Butane to defend.

So, the forums will live on and a diminished Ronway will be king of a crumbling rubble pile.

Again, this isn't a perfect plan; the real one will remain a secret until it is needed.

posts.name: Nielzabub
posts.cooked:
In the year 2021, Sentinels of the Multiverse has become an international sensation. For a while, it was a golden era of prosperity as nations learned to come together and team up to fight the villains of poverty and hunger instead of always fighting for each other. Alas, the peace ended as schisms between different play groups developed. Arguments erupted all around the world as people fought over who was the best hero and what house rules could be added to make the game better.

North America was split in half from the two largest warring factions led by the accursed Ronway and the deceptively delicious Brocolli.The accursed Ronway led the side that demanded that no house rules ever be added for they were unnecessary and spoiled the game. Although his main power base was in the states, he had a presence in England due to a shared hatred of house rules that was shared the influential Silverleaf and Matchstickman. The deceptively delicious Brocolli was of the side that house rules were okay but games using them should probably not be recorded in the statistics. he also had a very strong foothold in the States as well as strong supporters in England and an alliance with the corrupted Deputy of the Greater than Games initiative, Arenson 9. The war started when the stalemate was halted when Brocolli was assasinated by the nemesis of all deceptively delicious vegetables, the sneaky Rabit.

The followers of Brocolli blamed the brotherhood of the Ronway for their leader's demise and left the world of internet forums and retaliated with guns and bombs. The elusive Rabit was never caught or brought to justice. He and and his friend Pydro watched the conflict from space in the Marot's Folly ready to profit off the inevitable war.

The deadliest weapon that the Ronways had in their arsenal were their phalanxes of phantom clowns that would terrorize the populace in their creepy masks and cloaks. The last words their victims would hear as they lay dying in pools of their own blood were, "Fixer is a great hero."

Oddly enough two of the most powerful and influential members of the world wide Sentinels network, Nielzabub and Reckless, did not join the war as everyone expected. They hid out in a small unknown island in Japan waiting for the right moment to intervene. By the time the war ended they would end up eating 6,712 Bananae.

In the end, Ronway was betrayed by his British friends when audio of him blaming England for all of the world's problems and that he was planning to betray them after he had quelled the deceptively delicious Brocolli's followers. Matchstickman and Silverleaf assasinated the dreaded Ronway and took over his army of deadly, creepy clowns.

The Broccolites unleased their deadliest weapon, a bomb. Everyone had forgotten those things existed and were really caught by surprise. The Ronways remembered that they too probably had bombs somewhere and thus the world became a wasteland. Nielzabub and Reckless returned from their self imposed exile and began preaching the world over the true value of Sentinels. They dedicated themselves to reminding people that the game was supposed to bring us together and not tear us apart. The world learned its lesson and Sentinels once again brought about an age of harmony and understanding.

This one is easy, as I'm currently trying to balance a custom hero that is exactly the hero I always wanted to be.

Name is Shifty, and I'm a team guy, eventually.  Every Environment is my home base.  After discovering I had my unique powers I travelled all over the world having fun and playing with my abilities.  I got pretty good, and now I can imitate anything that is close to humanoid shape that I see, I even pulled off being a Velociraptor for a while (you have to be careful when you don't know the language).  I started impersonating wealthy and powerful people, but the suffering and injustice I saw eventually got to me, and despite my efforts a life of felonious fun lost its appeal.

Eventually I settled into a group of heroes that go around trying to be the A-Team all the time, we have a lot of fun, and we get to help people.  I like to joke around and impersonate my friends and enemies, and sometimes even plants, but leaves are really hard to pull off well.  My favorite pastimes include causing Mayhem in enemy bases, and Confusing Super Villains with my awesome impressions.

Name:  Shifty

HP:  28

Base Power:  Deal one target 1 melee damage.

Card Type unique to my deck:  Double Agent:  Ongoing, Limited, Morph.

When this card enters play return all other Morph cards to your hand.

Select a Villain target, Shifty gains all keywords that target has, and is treated as a villain target.

If a non-hero card would cause Shifty to deal damage he may redirect that damage to any target.

If a Hero would damage Shifty you may destroy this card instead.

"So, what does a drone do for fun around here?"  Shifty, Robot Rolecall.

Equipment:  Appropriated Weaponry

Power:  Deal one target 3 damage of a type listed on the same type of card as Shifty (hero, villain, environment)

If none are listed this card deals Melee damage.

If there is not a morph card in play this power may not be used.

"I'm sorry, was that your gun?"  Shifty, The Sincerest Form.

One Shot:  Here Boy

Select an Environment Target, any text that would occur at the end of the Environment phase occurs now.  If Shifty is an Environment target he may exclude Heroes from being targetted.

"Good T-Rex, C'mon boy."  Shifty, The Sincerest Form

Another Ongoing:  Team Up:  Ongoing, Limited, Morph

When this card enters play return all other Morph cards to your hand.

Select a Hero, when that Hero would take damage you may redirect it to shifty, when that hero would deal damage increase it by 1.

At the start of your turn you may select a different hero, only one may be affected by this card at a time.

"I'm Legacy, and I'm super boring."  Shifty, Shifting Loyalties #2.

Bonus One-Shot:  Orders From the Top

Select a non-character Villain Card, that card is treated as having no text until the start of your next turn.

Play the top card of the villain deck.

If Shifty is not a Villain Target the Villain Target with the highest HP deals Shifty 4 irreducible Melee damage.

"Red 17, The Eagle has Landed, Dispatch Falanges!"  Shifty, Shifting Loyalties #4.

It's not too interesting of a story actually. There is a game for the Playstation (even has a remake on the PSP that I wasn't too found of) called Tactics Ogre: Let Us Cling Together. These days, If Ronway is already taken on something, I tend to name it RonwayX or WickedRonway instead. As of right now, the only account I use semi-regularly that doesn't use Ronway is my GameFaqs account, which is DryuR. Bet you can't guess what the R stands for!

 

Before any of those names, for games I would name my character Rat. Or as I got a bit older and would giggle at swear words, I would use Damnrat. Monster Tamer was something I would use on the internet. There were a few more names inbetween Monster Tamer and Ronway, but during that time it was what ever I could think of at the time.

posts.name: McBehrer
posts.cooked:
OH time to talk about McBehrer!

 

So, I was in Forensics in High School. In case you don't know, it's kind of a catch-all for a number of performance-based competitions, including poetry/prose reading, improv acting, etc; some solo, some duets. One of them had me and a friend performing an improv scene, where we were given a setting and a cast of characters, and 15 minutes or so to create a scene; then we acted it out. In the scene, we were a couple of people in a bar; being very drunk, when asked my name, I started rambling about how I names were stupid and you should be called by something that fits you. "So... call me... Mc... Bear! Because... Mc is a name!"

"Because you're Scottish!"

"... Yeah, that too. And... Bear, because I'm big. And hairy.

... like a bear."

And I thought it was kind of a cool name, so I changed the spelling to seem more name-like, and it's been my username for things ever since.

 

I'll refrain from asking a question, as that question was for everyone, so more people can answer.

Old character name from way back in my early DnD career, indirectly. The character was a pirate called Scarlett Red (don't blame me, the GM named her) and I basically stole her concept and name for my character when I started LARPing. It involved a fair bit of red hair colouring and a large rubber sword...

Well Scarlett was supposed to be getting married to a character called Logan who was played by my then-real-life-boyfriend (okay, that's amazingly sad, but I was young and didn't know any better) except Logan got killed by a skeleton or something before that happened.

It was about that time I needed a new email address, and a character name seemed a good way to go. Problem was, scarlettred or variants on that were all taken, so I nicked Logan's surname and went scarlett silverleaf. And it was the Silverleaf bit that stuck rather than Scarlett - I even use it for my business name. Occasionally I add a number if silverleaf's taken.

So yeah. Embarrassing, but there you go.

My first name is Russell. (That matters later.) Got the nickname Rabbit in high school. When I got to college, I was on crutches for most of my freshman year and I ate a lot of salads (still do), so when one of the guys found out I had the nickname Rabbit in high school, it became a natural fit. It became so common, when my mom called the dorm and asked for Russell, she'd get confusion, but when she asked for Rabbit, the guys would immediately know who she was talking about. ![](upload://cMxHQaDq0kbGxwGJQa30HupNF6d.gif)

In our second-year apartment, we would write notes to each other about phone calls or other messages, planning for things coming up, etc., as we often went for extended periods without seeing each other (due to schedules, etc.). (Keep in mind this was before we had email.) Two of my roommates would spell my name as "Russel". I would harass them about how "it's spelled with two ls", but they decided to just stop using my name and started using Rabbit.

So, naturally, I had to explain that it was spelled with one b. ![](upload://o6ZCu1GhPWrOmMs2x4YSWSvAS0g.gif)

From that point on, it was my default name on anything online that needed one.

posts.name: arenson9
posts.cooked:
arenson, sure, but why 9? Well, long ago when the Internet was young, I had to pick a username and it occured to me that it would be cool to be able to keep using the same username as time goes by, but I'd seen how on AOL people often had to pick things like Smith373 because 372 other people were named Smith. I figured there wouldn't likely be nine other people who ever wanted arenson as a username, so if I just started with arenson9 I could probably always use it. So far, so good.

 

Shoulda chosen arenson5. 5 is the best number!

posts.name: Theta_Sigma
posts.cooked:
@everyone- Talk about your forum username.  What is its significance?  Why did you pick it?  Is it a common username for you or specific to the SotM forums?

 

Theta Sigma is the designation used by The Doctor while he was in the Time Lord Academy. It's not his real name.

I use it in a number of different places, but it's not my only username (not by a long shot). Interestingly, it gets shortened in different ways, depending on where I am using it. Sometimes it's 'Theta', other places it's 'Sigma' or T_S or other variants.

 

I pointed this out on a chatroom on Kongregate, and now I am 'Bob' there.
